title: Polite Ways to Ask for Help

vocabulary.example: I need some assistance with my car.

vocabulary.meaning_ar: يساعد شخصًا / يمدّ له يد العون
vocabulary.example: Could you give me a hand with these boxes?
Can you lend me a hand with the dishes?

vocabulary.meaning_en: help or agreement that you give someone
vocabulary.example: I need your support to finish this project.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something kind you do to help someone
vocabulary.note_ar: نقول do someone a favour وليس make. في الأمريكية: favor
vocabulary.note_en: We say "do someone a favour", not "make". US spelling: favor.
vocabulary.example: Can you do me a favour and pick me up tomorrow?

vocabulary.meaning_en: give some of your time or money to someone

vocabulary.example: These instructions are a bit tricky.

vocabulary.meaning_en: try hard to do something difficult
vocabulary.note_ar: struggle with + اسم / struggle to + فعل
vocabulary.note_en: struggle with + noun / struggle to + verb
vocabulary.example: I'm struggling with this maths problem.

vocabulary.note_en: too much trouble = too much effort
vocabulary.example: Would it be too much trouble to call me back?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small hole in a tyre
vocabulary.example: I got a puncture on the motorway.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a hole that lets water or gas come out
vocabulary.example: There's a small leak under the sink.

vocabulary.meaning_en: put the parts of something together
vocabulary.example: Can you help me assemble this cupboard?

vocabulary.meaning_en: take someone around a place so they can see it
vocabulary.meaning_ar: يأخذ شخصًا في جولة للتعرف على المكان
vocabulary.example: Would you mind showing me around the office?

fine_lines.title: do a favour ✓ vs make a favour ✗
fine_lines.explanation_ar: في الإنجليزية نقول دائمًا do someone a favour. قول make a favour خطأ شائع عند العرب.
fine_lines.explanation_en: In English we always say "do someone a favour". "Make a favour" is a common mistake.

examples.sentence: Could you do me a favour?
She did me a big favour.

fine_lines.title: Formal vs informal requests for help
words: Could you give me a hand?
fine_lines.explanation_ar: I need some assistance / I need your support رسمية، تناسب الطوارئ والعمل. Could you give me a hand? / Lend me a hand غير رسمية مع الأصدقاء والعائلة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "I need some assistance" and "I need your support" are formal (emergencies, work). "Could you give me a hand?" and "Lend me a hand" are informal (friends, family).

examples.sentence: My car has broken down. I need some assistance.

examples.word: Could you give me a hand?
examples.sentence: Could you give me a hand setting the table?

expressions.meaning_en: A very polite general request for help.
expressions.example: My hands are full. Would you mind helping me with the door?

expressions.meaning_en: A formal request, often in an emergency or at work.
expressions.example: My car has broken down. I need some assistance.

expressions.phrase: Could you give me a hand?
expressions.meaning_en: An informal request to friends or family.
expressions.example: Could you give me a hand? Dinner is almost ready.

expressions.meaning_en: A formal request for help or agreement.
expressions.example: I need your support to get this plan approved.

expressions.phrase: Could you / Will you do me a favour?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل يمكنك أن تسدي لي معروفًا؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asks someone to do something kind for you.
expressions.example: Could you do me a favour and pick me up tomorrow?

expressions.meaning_en: Asks if someone has knowledge to help you.
expressions.example: Do you know anything about laptops? Mine won't start.

expressions.meaning_en: Asks someone to show you a place or how to do something.
expressions.example: Would you mind showing me where the meeting rooms are?

expressions.meaning_en: Asks for a little of someone's time.
expressions.example: Could you spare a moment to go over this document with me?

expressions.phrase: This is tricky / difficult. Can you help me?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks for help with something difficult.
expressions.example: These instructions are tricky. Can you help me?

expressions.phrase: Would it be too much trouble to ask you to ...?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل سيكون من المزعج أن أطلب منك أن ...؟
expressions.example: Would it be too much trouble to ask you to turn the TV down?

expressions.phrase: I'm struggling with this. Can you help me?
expressions.meaning_ar: أجد صعوبة في هذا. هل يمكنك مساعدتي؟
expressions.meaning_en: Says you find something hard and need help.
expressions.example: I'm struggling with this formula. Can you help me?

expressions.phrase: Can you lend me a hand with this?
expressions.meaning_en: An informal, friendly request for help.
expressions.example: Can you lend me a hand with this box? It's heavy.

expressions.phrase: Sure. What do you want me to do?
expressions.meaning_en: A friendly reply to a request for help.
expressions.example: Could you do me a favour? — Sure. What do you want me to do?

expressions.phrase: Two sets of hands are better than one.
expressions.meaning_en: Says a job is easier with two people.
expressions.example: Let's carry it together. Two sets of hands are better than one.

expressions.phrase: I'm sorry to trouble you, but ...
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to start a request.
expressions.example: I'm sorry to trouble you, but I need help with this report.

grammar.title: Would you mind + -ing?
grammar.explanation_ar: بعد Would you mind نستخدم الفعل بـ ing. للموافقة نقول No, not at all (أي: لا أمانع).
grammar.explanation_en: After "Would you mind" use the -ing form. To say yes, answer "No, not at all" (= I don't mind).
examples: Would you mind showing me around?
Would you mind opening the door? — No, not at all.

grammar.title: Indirect questions are more polite
grammar.explanation_ar: البريطانيون لا يحبون الطلبات المباشرة مثل Help me. يستخدمون أسئلة غير مباشرة بـ Could you / Would you / Would it be too much trouble لتكون أكثر تهذيبًا.
grammar.explanation_en: British speakers avoid direct orders like "Help me". They use indirect questions with Could you / Would you / Would it be too much trouble to sound polite.
examples: Help me. → Could you give me a hand?
Show me the office. → Would you mind showing me the office?
Turn it down. → Would it be too much trouble to ask you to turn it down?

grammar.title: struggle with + noun / struggle to + verb
grammar.explanation_ar: struggle with يأتي بعده اسم، وstruggle to يأتي بعده فعل.
grammar.explanation_en: Use "struggle with" + noun and "struggle to" + verb.
examples: I'm struggling to carry this box.

questions.question: Which is the most FORMAL?
choices: Could you give me a hand?
questions.explanation_ar: I need some assistance عبارة رسمية.

Could you lend me some money?
questions.explanation_ar: spare a moment = يمنح القليل من وقته.
questions.explanation_en: "Spare a moment" = give a little time.

questions.question: "Can you lend me a hand?" means:
choices: Can you give me a glove?

questions.question: You're new at work. You ask a colleague:
choices: Would you mind showing me around?
Would you mind to show me around?
Would you mind show me around?
Would you mind shown me around?
questions.explanation_ar: بعد Would you mind نستخدم showing.

questions.question: "These instructions are tricky" means they are:
Your car breaks down on the motorway. You phone for help and say:
choices: Could you do me a favour?
Lend me a hand with this.
questions.explanation_ar: في الطوارئ نستخدم العبارة الرسمية I need some assistance.
questions.explanation_en: In an emergency use the formal "I need some assistance".

questions.question: Would you mind opening the window? — "___" (You are happy to do it.)
questions.explanation_ar: No, not at all تعني لا أمانع، أي سأفعل ذلك.
questions.explanation_en: "No, not at all" means you don't mind, so you will do it.
